scope: Convergence check at head 21ef362 on origin/main 6a416df: whether round 2's R6-R10 are discharged, plus collateral from the round-2 repair and the rebase.

round_2_status.R6: discharged for the DETACH case (no-op + detached frame + decoy no longer earns a postcondition) — but NOT for the class: R11 shows a frame re-navigated IN PLACE reopens it
round_2_status.R7: discharged for wall-clock seconds; NOT discharged for the case count of the same republish (R12)
round_2_status.R8: band now publishes the ledger maximum with the disclosure restored — but the repair moved README's baseline onto a red report (R13)

circuit_breaker: Fired. Three review rounds without approval. Escalated to the human per the pr-loop protocol rather than opening round 4 unilaterally.

findings.claim: R6's guard closes the detach door but not the class: when the page re-renders the acted frame IN PLACE (same <iframe> element, new document) instead of removing it, Frame.is_detached() stays False, check_state reads the successor document as if it were the acted one, and a literal no-op click again records postcondition_ok: true — falsifying ADR-036's Ruling sentence that the predicates are 'evaluated in exactly ONE document: the one resolve returned the step's target from'.
findings.evidence:
src/browser/agent.py:557 (detached() tests is_detached, i.e. frame-object liveness, never document identity) and :632 (the None guard fires only on that test); src/browser/resolver.py:460 returns the Frame OBJECT as scope, and agent.py:606/611 evaluate the predicates in whatever document that frame currently hosts. Measured on this tree: src/browser/fixtures/frames-decoy-detach.html with its timer line changed from document.getElementById('w').innerHTML = '' to document.querySelector('#w iframe').srcdoc = '

Filing loaded

' — same page-owned timer scheduled at LOAD, same empty click handler. Probe output: scope about:srcdoc / check_state -> True / detached False. Verified with the decoy iframe deleted too, so the True comes from the successor document inside the acted frame, which the click never touched. ADR-036:6 and the §1 table row at :39 assert this cannot happen; §4 declares only the DETACH case. No case in any suite can go red on it.
findings.repro: resolve the in-frame button, click it, then check_state(page, {'text_visible':'Filing loaded'}, scope=<that Frame>) against the srcdoc-swap variant of the fixture -> True with is_detached() False
findings.acceptance: Either the scope test becomes document-identity-based rather than frame-object-based (a frame whose document changed under the step is as unverifiable as one that detached), or ADR-036 §1/§4 state plainly that the ruling scopes to a FRAME and that a frame re-navigated by the page between action and check reopens §1's hazard in full — with a committed adversarial case pinning whichever outcome is chosen.

findings.claim: R7 is discharged for the wall-clock seconds but not for the case COUNT of the same republish: three surfaces say the invariant band was re-derived at 89 cases while ADR-019 §3, README and the runner all say 90.
findings.evidence: ADR-029:6 ('invariant is 30s at 89 cases, re-derived by the same rule and republished in ADR-019 §3'); INDEX.md:39 ('re-derived again at 89 by PR #66 R6-R8'); fast-wall-clock-budget.json:169 ('the band was re-derived at 89 cases'). Against ADR-019:306 (90 cases, ts 20260828-033258, 26.02s, 89/90), README.md:183 (| invariant | 90 | 26.02s | 29.92 | 30s |) and load_cases('invariant') == 90. All three 89s are text this branch added; nothing grades them — the same green-disagreement mechanism R7 named.
findings.repro: python -c "from evals.run import load_cases; print(len(load_cases('invariant')))" -> 90 ; grep -n 'at 89 cases\|again at 89' specs/decisions/ADR-029-local-fast-ceiling-105.md specs/decisions/INDEX.md evals/adversarial/fast-wall-clock-budget.json

findings.claim: The 'None is loud' claim holds only for {click, press, go_back}: on any other verb an authored expected_state whose acted frame dies is now silently unverified, where the same input previously produced a graded True/False.
findings.evidence: agent.py:632 returns None for every action, but verifier.py:419 STATE_CHANGING = {click, press, go_back} and :498-504 flag null only for those; fill/select_option/scroll are protected because agent.py:1203/1258/1288 set postcondition_ok = True by readback before the check, but extract/extract_all/observe carry neither. An extract step whose authored text_visible is genuinely absent AND whose acted frame detaches records postcondition_ok: null, no_failed_postcondition no longer sees it, and the run answers. ADR-036 §4:104-108 names the three verbs but does not state that other steps' nulls are silent.
findings.repro: the committed postcondition-scope-detached-by-its-own-action fixture with the step's action changed from click to extract and a target in the detaching frame: trace records postcondition_ok: null and the run does not fail semantic
findings.acceptance: Either ADR-036 §4 states the residual explicitly (a null from a dead scope is loud only for the state-changing verbs), or the null is graded for any step that AUTHORED an expected_state, with a case pinning whichever is chosen.
